newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 25.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 25.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - The New York State Attorney General calls on Reynolds Tobacco to drop its sexy new advertising campaign for Camel cigarettes and urges Philip Morris to stop using the "Marlboro Man" in its advertising. The new Camel campaign -- replacing the controversial Joe Camel cartoon figure -- carries the theme "What you're looking for" and features glamorous women models.

ABIDJAN - Boom times are bringing top ad agencies to Africa. Ogilvy & Mather, part of WPP Group Plc, has forged an alliance with Ocean ad agency in Ivory Coast and Ocean's big local rival, Panafcom, is linking up with another global leader, Young & Rubicam.

KARLSRUHE, Germany - A German court has decided that local Benetton retailers are not entitled to compensation for losses in turnover they blamed on Benetton's shock-style advertising campaign of the early 1990s.

LONDON - The media-buying and media-planning business -- long treated as the ugly stepchild of the advertising industry -- has finally come into its own, driven by a proliferation in media and a trend by advertisers toward globalisation. As a result, advertising industry executives say they expect consolidation in the sector to meet the trend.

MEXICO CITY - Political campaigning and pension fund advertising boosted second quarter revenues from television commercials at Mexico's Televisa by 24.6 percent over the year-ago quarter. "This increase primarily reflects revenues from sales of advertising under the company's French Plan," Televisa says. Under the French Plan, advertisers pay Televisa the following year's advertising ahead of time, usually in the fall.

SEATTLE - Microsoft Corp plans to increase significantly spending on sales, marketing and development over the coming year, a move that could crimp earnings growth for the software giant until two major new products are launched in 1998.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
BRUSSELS - The European Commission threatens to take Spain to court over a law on decoders for digital pay-TV services that it says restricts free trade.
ROME - Italian communications group Mediaset is close to concluding a deal on a digital platform for television, its chairman says.

MUNICH - Bavarian media tycoon Leo Kirch, one of German television industry's most guarded figures, is lifting the veil of secrecy that shrouds his media empire and introducing a new policy of openess say industry observers.

LOS ANGELES - A new pop culture magazine called Gear and aimed at young males is set to compete with the likes of Rolling Stone and Details when it hits newsstands next year, its publisher Bob Guccione Jr says.

LONDON - Yahoo! UK, a provider of Internet search engines, says a new survey dispels the myth that Internet users are "lonely nerds," showing them instead to be active, affluent adults who use the Internet for work and leisure.

ALBANY, Texas - An old-timers' bid to pull the plug on MTV in this small Texas town has sparked a generational battle with its young music fans. Upset by sexual innuendo and raw language on the MTV cable music video channel, 650 Albany residents sign a petition asking that it be dropped from the local cable line-up.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

GREENWICH, Connecticut - UST Inc says its subsidiary, United States Tobacco Co, has debuted a series of new marketing and sales initiatives intended to help address the competitive situation in the marketplace. These initiatives include the introduction of its Red Seal smokeless tobacco.

HARARE - Carl Ware, Coca Cola senior vice-president and president of the company's Africa Group, says that political and economic reforms in Africa are attractive to foreign investors and that Coca Cola expects to double its business in Africa in the next five years.

JAKARTA - A programme to boost tea consumption in Indonesia, Slovakia, Zimbabwe and Spain will be launched next January by the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation an industry official says. *********
HERZOGENAURACH, Germany - German sportswear group Puma AG expects sales growth below 10 percent this year after turnover climbed six percent in the first half.
STOCKHOLM - Sweden's mobile phone company AB LM Ericsson delivered surprisingly good first-half results on Thursday, boosted by a sharp increase in sales of mobile handsets.

ORLANDO, Florida - Planet Hollywood International Inc says that it and AMC Entertainment Inc have formed a joint venture to develop, own and operate an integrated movie-going, dining and retail concept worldwide.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - Motown hits from the Seventies are the best music to make love to, young Britons say in a Gallup survey. "Magic Motown moments are the best records to make love to," Gallup says. Among modern singers, American Jon Bon Jovi and Britain's Louise topped the poll as the sexiest performers.

FRANKFURT - Rolls-Royce, a badge of wealth and privilege on four wheels, hopes to be a bit more politically correct with its first totally new model in nearly two decades that is due by the turn of the century. Rolls-Royce Motor Cars says it wants the new model to have "more socially acceptable shapes".
BUCHAREST - Romanian members of parliament are to be given mobile phones at taxpayers' expense to enable staff to track them down and cut absenteeism in sessions, a Bucharest daily newspaper says.

BEIJING - Smoking kills half a million people a year in China and the country's huge population of puffers is costing it billions of dollars in tobacco-related losses, a United Nations health official says.
